events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Windward side of Honolulu County...

* WHEN...Until 930 PM HST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding on roads, poor drainage areas, and in
streams. Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 718 PM HST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain over areas of windward Oahu. Rain was falling at a
rate of 0.5 to 1.5 inches per hour in the Kaneohe Bay and Kailua
areas. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in
the advisory area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Kaneohe, Kailua, Ahuimanu, Kahaluu, Waiahole, and Waikane.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking waves
of 12 to 18 feet expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large
breaking waves of 7 to 10 feet expected in the surf zone. For the
Coastal Flood Statement, isolated minor coastal flooding up to 1
foot expected. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents expected.

* WHERE...North and east facing reefs of Tinian and Saipan.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning and Coastal Flood Statement, from
1 AM to 4 PM ChST Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM
Friday to 4 PM ChST Saturday. For the High Rip Current Risk, from
late tonight through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Some water on low lying roads and property. Breaking
waves can sweep people off jetties and docks, and into dangerous
seas. Life-threatening swimming conditions and significant beach
erosion can be expected. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...As TY In-fa moves west-northwest toward the
far northern CNMI, seas are expected to rapidly increase due to the
large, long-period northeast swell emanating from In-fa. This will
produce dangerous surf along north and east facing reefs after
midnight tonight. As In-fa progresses, swell will become north,
then northwest, resulting in surf building over west facing reefs
Friday night. Surf will remain hazardous through Saturday
afternoon. These surf conditions will maintain a high risk of
dangerous rip currents.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal
flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 1 PM PDT Thursday.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 1 PM Thursday to 2 PM PDT
Friday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Coastal residents and managers of
infrastructure in the warned/advisory area should prepare for
rising water and take appropriate action to protect life and
property. Highest tides will occur around 11 AM on Thursday
and noon on Friday. Observed high tides are 1.4 to 1.6 feet
above astronomical tide predictions.
